title: B2 Writing Quiz 1 — Environment & Climate Change

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If we had invested in renewable energy earlier, we wouldn't be facing this crisis now.
If we invested in renewable energy earlier, we wouldn't be facing this crisis now.
If we had invested in renewable energy earlier, we wouldn't have faced this crisis now.
If we had invested in renewable energy earlier, we won't face this crisis now.
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: If + past perfect (past condition), would + base verb (present result): 'If we had invested..., we wouldn't be facing... now.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The situation will get worse unless governments won't take action now.
The situation will get worse unless governments take action now.
The situation will get worse unless that governments take action now.
The situation will get worse without governments take action now.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if...not' and is followed by an affirmative clause: 'unless governments take action now.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Several new environmental laws has been passed this year.
Several new environmental laws have passed this year.
Several new environmental laws have been passed this year.
Several new environmental laws have being passed this year.
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive: have/has been + past participle: 'have been passed this year.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This pollution problem should solved immediately.
This pollution problem should being solved immediately.
This pollution problem should be solve immediately.
This pollution problem should be solved immediately.
questions.explanation: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle: 'should be solved immediately.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "Please reduce your plastic use.")
options: The activist told us to reduce our plastic use.
The activist told us reduce our plastic use.
The activist said us to reduce our plastic use.
The activist told us that reduce our plastic use.
questions.explanation: Reported commands: tell + object + to + base verb: 'told us to reduce our plastic use.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "You should recycle more.")
options: She suggested to recycle more.
She suggested recycling more.
She suggested me recycling more.
She suggested that I recycling more.
questions.explanation: 'Suggest' is followed by a gerund or 'that + subject + base verb': 'suggested recycling more.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The organization which she volunteers for it protects endangered species.
The organization for that she volunteers protects endangered species.
The organization for which she volunteers protects endangered species.
The organization she volunteers for which protects endangered species.
questions.explanation: In formal style, the preposition moves before 'which': 'the organization for which she volunteers.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The report publishing last week revealed shocking data.
The report published last week reveal shocking data.
The report which published last week revealed shocking data.
The report published last week revealed shocking data.
questions.explanation: A passive meaning reduces 'which was published' to the past participle alone: 'The report published last week...'

questions.topic: Modal verbs of past deduction (must have)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The factory must have released toxic chemicals into the river.
The factory must released toxic chemicals into the river.
The factory must have release toxic chemicals into the river.
The factory must has released toxic chemicals into the river.
questions.explanation: Past deduction: must have + past participle: 'must have released toxic chemicals.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The government should acted sooner to prevent the flooding.
The government should have acted sooner to prevent the flooding.
The government should have act sooner to prevent the flooding.
The government should has acted sooner to prevent the flooding.
questions.explanation: Past regret/criticism: should have + past participle: 'should have acted sooner.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Global temperatures rose significantly over the past century.
Global temperatures has risen significantly over the past century.
Global temperatures have risen significantly over the past century.
Global temperatures have rose significantly over the past century.
questions.explanation: 'Over the past century' links the past to the present, so present perfect is used: 'have risen significantly.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: By the time scientists warned us, the ice caps already started melting.
By the time scientists had warned us, the ice caps already started melting.
By the time scientists warned us, the ice caps have already started melting.
By the time scientists warned us, the ice caps had already started melting.
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect: 'the ice caps had already started melting.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Environmental leaders are meeting next week to discuss new policies.
Environmental leaders meet next week to discuss new policies.
Environmental leaders will meeting next week to discuss new policies.
Environmental leaders are meet next week to discuss new policies.
questions.explanation: Present continuous expresses a fixed future arrangement: 'are meeting next week.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She said she will attend the climate summit.
She said she would attend the climate summit.
She said she would attended the climate summit.
She said she would have attend the climate summit.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'will' shifts back to 'would': 'she said she would attend the summit.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I wish we take climate change more seriously.
I wish we have taken climate change more seriously.
I wish we took climate change more seriously.
I wish we would take climate change more seriously as a society.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' + past simple expresses regret about a present situation: 'I wish we took climate change more seriously.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I wish scientists warned us earlier about the risks.
I wish scientists have warned us earlier about the risks.
I wish scientists would have warned us earlier about the risks.
I wish scientists had warned us earlier about the risks.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' + past perfect expresses regret about the past: 'I wish scientists had warned us earlier.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We had solar panels installed on our roof last year.
We had installed solar panels on our roof last year.
We had solar panels install on our roof last year.
We have solar panels installed on our roof last year.
questions.explanation: Causative form: have + object + past participle shows someone else did the action: 'had solar panels installed.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Never before the region had experienced such severe droughts.
Never before had the region experienced such severe droughts.
Never before did the region experienced such severe droughts.
Never before has the region had experienced such severe droughts.
questions.explanation: Negative adverbials at the start trigger inversion: 'Never before had the region experienced...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The committee is looking the causes of the oil spill into.
The committee is looking in to the causes of the oil spill.
The committee is looking into the causes of the oil spill.
The committee is looking into to the causes of the oil spill.
questions.explanation: 'Look into' means 'investigate' and is inseparable: 'looking into the causes.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: What we urgently need are a global agreement on emissions.
That we urgently need is a global agreement on emissions.
What we urgently need is global agreement on emissions it.
What we urgently need is a global agreement on emissions.
questions.explanation: 'What' clefts take a singular verb when the complement is singular: 'What we need is a global agreement.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Some countries have reduced emissions, whereas others continue to increase them.
Some countries have reduced emissions, whereas others continues to increase them.
Some countries have reduced emissions whereas, others continue to increase them.
Some countries have reduced emissions despite others continue to increase them.
questions.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two clauses and is followed directly by the subject: 'whereas others continue...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: In spite the new regulations, pollution levels remain high.
In spite of the new regulations, pollution levels remain high.
Despite of the new regulations, pollution levels remain high.
In spite of the new regulations, pollution levels remain high though.
questions.explanation: 'In spite of' is followed by a noun phrase: 'In spite of the new regulations, pollution levels remain high.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: A number of studies has linked plastic waste to marine life decline.
The number of studies have linked plastic waste to marine life decline.
A number of studies have linked plastic waste to marine life decline.
A great number of studies has linked plastic waste to marine life decline.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' + plural noun takes a plural verb: 'a number of studies have linked...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She spoke in behalf of the entire environmental coalition.
She spoke on behalf for the entire environmental coalition.
She spoke behalf of the entire environmental coalition.
She spoke on behalf of the entire environmental coalition.
questions.explanation: 'On behalf of' means 'representing someone': 'she spoke on behalf of the coalition.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The implementation of stricter regulations reduced carbon emissions significantly.
The implement of stricter regulations reduced carbon emissions significantly.
The implementing of stricter regulations reduced carbon emissions significantly.
The implementation of stricter regulations reduce carbon emissions significantly.
questions.explanation: Formal writing often nominalizes verbs into nouns: 'implement' becomes 'the implementation of...'

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate formal opening line for an email requesting information about a recycling program?
options: I'm writing to ask you about your organization's recycling initiatives, ok?
I am writing to enquire about your organization's recycling initiatives.
Just wanted to know about your organization's recycling initiatives.
Hey, tell me about your organization's recycling initiatives.
questions.explanation: 'I am writing to enquire about...' is a standard formal opening for information requests.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate opening line for a formal complaint about a factory's waste disposal?
options: I'm writing because I'm really mad about the factory's waste disposal methods.
I want to complain about the factory's waste disposal methods, it's bad.
I am writing to express my concern about the factory's waste disposal methods.
I am writing to express my concern about the factory's waste disposal methods, ok.
questions.explanation: Formal complaints use measured language such as 'I am writing to express my concern about...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The results of the study were extreme alarming.
The results of the study were extremely alarm.
The results of the study were very much alarming.
The results of the study were extremely alarming.
questions.explanation: 'Extremely' (adverb) modifies the adjective 'alarming': 'were extremely alarming.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Renewable energy is cheaper. Moreover, it produces no emissions.
Renewable energy is cheaper, moreover it produces no emissions.
Renewable energy is cheaper. Moreover it produces no emissions.
Renewable energy is cheaper moreover, it produces no emissions.
questions.explanation: 'Moreover' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma: 'Renewable energy is cheaper. Moreover, it produces no emissions.'

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: You'd support stronger climate policies, didn't you?
You'd support stronger climate policies, wouldn't you?
You'd support stronger climate policies, would you?
You'd support stronger climate policies, wouldn't it?
questions.explanation: A positive statement with 'would' takes a negative tag: 'You'd support..., wouldn't you?'
